name: Cover System
description: Owns the relationship between a character and cover geometry: snapping to a cover edge, leaning or peeking, and the exposure fraction that everything downstream reads. It does not reduce damage itself — it publishes exposureFraction and combat.damage_resolver applies it, because mitigation math already has one home and a second one guarantees the two drift apart. Cover volumes are level data, not components; this queries them through the character's own spatial context. Moving along cover is still movement.run_control's velocity — this component only constrains which directions are legal while attached, so detaching (or a dash) returns full steering with no state to unwind.

inputs.name: snapDistance
inputs.description: How close to a cover edge the attach request reaches. Too generous and players magnetize across doorways; too tight and cover feels unapproachable. Tuned against movement.run_control's top speed, not in isolation.

inputs.name: peekExposureFraction
inputs.description: Fraction of the hittable profile presented while leaning out to fire. The peek is the core cover transaction — safety traded for shots — so this number, not damage, is where cover balance lives.

inputs.name: crouchExposureFraction
inputs.description: Exposure while hunkered behind low cover. Lower than peek because hunkering yields no shots; if the two are equal, no one ever hunkers.

inputs.name: detachOnSprint
inputs.description: Whether a sprint input breaks cover instantly. True, because a sprint that fails while attached to cover reads as ignored input — the same fairness rule as jump buffering, applied to leaving safety.

outputs.name: inCover
outputs.description: True while attached to a cover edge. AI reads this to decide flanking; the HUD reads it for the lean prompt.

outputs.name: exposureFraction
outputs.description: Current hittable fraction, 0 to 1, blending between hunker and peek. This is the single number combat.damage_resolver consumes — cover is one multiplier, not a rules engine.
